Martyna Wojciechowska talks to Morena Herrera, who fights for women's rights in El Salvador.The country ranks first in terms of the number of murders of women.About 500 such cases are reported annually, with a population of less than 3 million.More than half of the victims of violence do not seek help and do not reveal the truth even to their closest family members.Moreover, El Salvador has one of the most restrictive anti-abortion laws in the world.Termination of pregnancy is always illegal.If a woman loses a child in unclear circumstances, she immediately becomes a suspect.The penalty for her ranges from 2 to 8 years, and if found guilty, she may be imprisoned for 50 years.A doctor can be sentenced to 6 to 12 years for performing an abortion.Anyone who knew about the situation but did not inform the authorities is also complicit.

Martyna Wojciechowska breaks stereotypes.In the Wodaabe community of Chad, men court women.For this reason, they attach great importance to their appearance.They put on their best clothes and do their makeup.Their chosen ones are only supposed to observe and then decide.The best place to look for a husband is the Gerewol Festival.The episode's heroine, Fatima, chose Haire last year.According to tradition, their wedding should take place on the anniversary of the happy event.A few months ago, the woman gave birth to a daughter.They only see each other in secret, because only such meetings are allowed.A man can have several wives, but he must pay appropriately for a good partner.Among the Wodaabe, the greatest wealth is cows.Haire's parents gave five cows and several million Central African francs for Fatima.

Martyna Wojciechowska spent six hundred and fifty days traveling, during which she visited fifty countries.This is how eighty episodes of the program were created.Over the ten years of the series, she has made many new friends, and many of the characters still hold a special place in her heart.They include Kabula - an albino girl from Tanzania.Thanks to the money collected by viewers and the "Between Heaven and Earth" foundation, she was able to fulfill her dreams.She started studying at a private school in Mwanza.Now he is doing everything he can to become a lawyer and defend the rights of people with albinism.She spent her last holidays in Poland, with Martyna Wojciechowska.Viewers will see how this first visit went.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska once again sets out on a fascinating journey to learn about different aspects of the lives of women living in distant corners of the world.Some of the points of the route in this edition will be India, Senegal, South Korea, South Africa, Israel and Mexico.The program participants will talk about their everyday lives and reveal intimate secrets to the traveler.Some of them will be truly moving.This season, the journalist will look at how the Orthodox Jewish community functions on a daily basis and how they celebrate the joyful holiday of Purim.He will visit a nursing home for women who were once involved in prostitution.Although this profession is legal in Mexico, women are not entitled to any benefits.The traveler will also meet teenage Karolina, who works almost 24 hours a day at a garbage dump, and in South Africa she will meet a girl who dives with sharks.These are just some of the many amazing experiences that await Martyna Wojciechowska Martyna Wojciechowska visits South Korea, a country that has one of the lowest fertility rates in the world.According to research, as much as 90 percentmen and 80 percentwomen between 25 and 30 are single.Women fear that marriage and pregnancy will stand in the way of their advancement at work and will be a reason for discrimination.On the other hand, South Korea is a conservative country and almost every woman wants to get married.For this reason, the business of solo weddings is booming here.It turns out that young Korean women do not even need a partner to fulfill their dreams of a white dress and a veil.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Malta is a small but picturesque island country located in the Mediterranean Sea.Every year, makeshift boats and rafts come to its shores, bringing over three thousand refugees fleeing war, hunger and human trafficking.Only the strongest survive the journey in terrible conditions.Then they have to drift for up to forty days along the sea border because no one wants to accept them.Martyna Wojciechowska meets Hermon from war-torn Eritrea, and Agnes from Zimbabwe.The former did not intend to come to Europe, but when she became pregnant, she had no choice - it was the only way to ensure the safety of herself and her daughter.The second was a victim of human trafficking.She hasn't seen her children for five years.She works hard to become independent and create a new home for her family.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: This is the unique, 100th edition of the program whose main character is Elżbieta Dzikowska.She is a sinologist, journalist, art historian and photographer, but she is most famous as a traveler.Together with Tony Halik, she discovered the farthest, wildest corners of the Earth for Poles at a time when they practically could not cross the border of their country.It was she who made Martyna Wojciechowska, who was just a few years old, start dreaming about expeditions.Many years later, the women met and became friends, but so far they have not had the opportunity to go on a journey together.Now the situation has changed, and the destination of the escapade is Podlasie.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: This season was special in many ways.It included the 100th anniversary episode, produced for the first time in Poland.At the same time, this series was considered the most difficult, because due to the pandemic, Martyna Wojciechowska had to stay in the country for four months, and further photos might not have been taken at all.However, for both the traveler and her heroines, the impossible does not exist.In the last episode, viewers will learn about the behind-the-scenes of the program, prepared during the pandemic.Despite the border closure, the team traveled a distance equal to one length of the equator, meeting truly extraordinary women.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: The Roma live in most countries, but do not have their own country.According to estimates, there are from 8 to 15 million of them in the world, and in Romania - from about 500,000 to 2 million.Among the many Roma communities, we can mention the Gabors, who traditionally have the same surname to honor the Hungarian king from whom they received rights in the 17th century.They are referred to as aristocracy due to their light skin and financial status.They are distinguished by their attachment to tradition and the Adventist church.Men wear hats and mustaches.If they do not have the latter, it means that they have renounced their origins.Women, on the other hand, must hide their hair from marriage until death, and cannot wear makeup, lipstick or long nails.Their beauty lies in their naturalness.Although individual families traditionally pursue specific professions, they run the home.Martyna Wojciechowska, however, meets Rosalina in Transylvania, who is learning crafts in her future father-in-law's workshop.
